_strings.@@1e90561d597b: Tuition Tax Credit — A SC resident student (or a parent/legal guardian/other person who can claim the student as a dependent and who paid the tuition) attending a qualifying SC 2-year or 4-year college/university. Student must have received an SC high school diploma (or qualifying homeschool/out-of-state prep diploma) during or after May 2018, enrolled within 12 months of graduating high school, qualify for in-state tuition, be a degree-seeking undergraduate (or in a qualifying 1-year certificate/diploma program), and complete at least 30 credit hours for the year (15 if attending only one semester; 12 at Converse/Wofford). Disqualifiers include being in student-loan default, receiving a LIFE or Palmetto Fellows Scholarship for both Spring and Fall, certain felony/alcohol/drug convictions, and claiming for more than four consecutive years after enrollment.

_strings.@@5d8aba77dbaf: Two Wage Earner Credit — Married couples filing jointly where both spouses have earned income taxed to South Carolina. Not allowed for filing statuses Single, Married Filing Separately, or Head of Household. If either spouse's qualified earned income is zero or less, the credit cannot be taken.
_strings.@@74fdcd4b0ca3: 2023 South Carolina Individual Income Tax Tables SC1040TT (Revised 4/4/23) — the mandatory tax tables for taxable income under $100,000 and the '2023 Tax Rate Schedule for taxable income of $100,000 or more' ('1. Multiply the amount on line 5 by 6.4%; 2. Subtract $670', with the worked example $101,000 -> $5,794); 2023 SC1040 Instructions Line 6 ('If your income subject to tax on line 5 is less than $100,000, use the SC1040TT... If ... $100,000 or more, use the tax rate schedule') and Line w (dependent exemption $4,610). Second pass (bracket bounds and constants): 2023 SC4972, '2023 Tax Computation Schedule' — $0 to $3,330: 0% times the amount; $3,330 to $16,680: 3% times the amount minus $100; $16,680 or more: 6.4% times the amount minus $670 (https://dor.sc.gov/sites/dor/files/forms/SC4972_2023.pdf); corroborated by the SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office 2023 State IIT Comparisons Report (Tax Year 2023: >$0 0%, >$3,330 3%, >$16,680 6.4%; rfa.sc.gov).
_strings.@@d8ee2b9ea0e0: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Full-year SC residents who incurred federal child and dependent care expenses (reported on federal Form 2441). Part-year residents/nonresidents qualify only if they are residents of a state that offers a comparable credit to nonresidents, and then only on a prorated basis. Cannot be claimed if filing status is Married Filing Separately.
_strings.@@eac696fb9f90: South Carolina Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — Full-year South Carolina residents who were eligible for and claimed the federal Earned Income Tax Credit on their federal return for the same tax year. The TC-60 instructs the taxpayer to STOP (no credit) if they were not a full-year SC resident or were not eligible for the federal EITC.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.
_strings.@@f20915ce4653: Treaty conformity — SC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from SC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the SC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: SC1040 line 1 starts from FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME ("Enter your taxable income from your federal form" - 2023 SC1040 Instructions, p.2). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal taxable income before the SC return begins. SC's additions to income (SC1040 lines a-e) do NOT include any add-back of tax-treaty-exempt income. The only foreign-related add-back is on line e ("Add back foreign area allowances, cost of living allowances, and income from US possessions"), which is distinct from income exempt under a federal income tax treaty and does not re-capture treaty income. Because treaty-exempt income is neither in the federal taxable-income starting point nor added back, it is NOT re-taxed by SC -> conforms. (SC also confirms conformity to the IRC as amended through 12/31/2022 except as otherwise provided.)

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2023 Form SC1040, line 6: 'TAX on your South Carolina Income Subject to Tax (see SC1040TT)'. Line 5 (South Carolina Income Subject to Tax) = line 1 federal taxable income ('Enter federal taxable income from your federal form') + line 2 SC additions (lines a-e) - line 4 SC subtractions (lines f-w, including the line w dependent exemption this block ships). This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: supply SC1040 line 5 (South Carolina Income Subject to Tax) BEFORE the line w dependent exemption — i.e. line 1 federal TAXABLE income (federal 1040 line 15; the federal standard/itemized deduction is already embedded, never subtract it again) plus SC additions (lines a-e) minus the other SC subtractions (lines f-v) — and pass dependents_count so the op subtracts the shipped $4,610-per-dependent line w amount to reproduce line 5. South Carolina has NO personal exemption and NO state standard deduction of its own. Adjudication note (two-pass): pass 1 = the 2023 SC1040TT (mandatory tables below $100,000 + the printed $100,000-or-more schedule '6.4% minus $670'); pass 2 = the 2023 SC4972's printed '2023 Tax Computation Schedule' ($0-$3,330 0%; $3,330-$16,680 3% times the amount minus $100; $16,680+ 6.4% times the amount minus $670), corroborated by the SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office 2023 report (>$0 0%, >$3,330 3%, >$16,680 6.4%). Both passes agree on every bound and rate. NOTE: the SC1040 instruction booklet itself prints NO bracket dollar bounds — the SC4972 schedule is the official in-form statement of them. CRITICAL — SC's filed arithmetic is a SUBTRACTION METHOD, not marginal accumulation: the official computation is 'rate x ENTIRE income - constant', and the printed constants are ROUNDED in the taxpayer's favor ($100 vs the exact marginal $99.90; $670 vs the exact $667.02). Pure marginal accumulation (this engine) therefore comes out UP TO $2.98 + rounding HIGHER than the filed method above $16,680 — e.g. $101,000 -> engine $5,797 vs the SC1040TT's own printed example $5,794 (6.4% x $101,000 - $670). The filed return must use the SC1040TT table or the $100,000+ schedule; treat this block's output as an estimate within $3. Tax-table mandate: taxable income under $100,000 MUST use the SC1040TT tax tables (2023 SC1040 instructions, Line 6); the tables are built in $50/$100 bands from the subtraction formulas at band midpoints, so a row can differ from exact arithmetic by a few dollars in either direction (e.g. exact $12,000 -> engine $260, but the $12,000-$12,100 row prints $262; $16,800-$16,900 prints $408 vs engine $409 at $16,805). Taxable income of $100,000 or more MUST use the rate schedule (6.4% x line 5 - $670). ONE rate schedule for every filing status — the SC1040TT states 'Use this Tax Rate Schedule for any filing status claimed on the SC1040'; the identical schedule is duplicated across all four statuses here, copied, not derived (qualifying surviving spouse included). Zero-rate floor: the first $3,330 of SC taxable income is taxed at 0% (the schema's zero-rate bottom bracket, like OH/MS) — a filer at or below $3,330 owes $0 with no exemption needed. Credits are NOT modeled (tax credits, not base reductions): Two Wage Earner Credit (line 12, .007 x up to $50,000 of the lower-earning spouse's qualified earned income, max $350), Child and Dependent Care Credit (line 11, 7% of the federal expense, max $210/$420), SC Earned Income Tax Credit (125% of the federal EITC via TC-60 -> SC1040TC -> line 13, nonrefundable), and the refundable Tuition Tax Credit (line 21, Form I-319). Out of scope on the same return: TAX on Lump-Sum Distribution (line 7, SC4972) is a separate additional tax; Active Trade or Business income electing the flat 3% rate (Form I-335) is excluded from this schedule; both are computed on their own forms.
